records.proposition: In 16 metformin-treated adults with type 2 diabetes, the tested carbohydrate-last meal order lowered three-hour glucose iAUC and incremental peak versus carbohydrate first.
records.studyContext: Randomised three-condition crossover, one week apart; 30-minute matched meal: 10-minute first course, 10-minute interval, 10-minute second course. Chicken and salad before bread/orange juice versus reverse; sandwich condition also tested. Venous sampling through 180 minutes; mixed models with multiplicity adjustment and missing-sandwich sensitivity analysis.

rationale.D: Exact acute meal/glucose proposition is directly measured; this D2 does not transfer to long-term variability.
rationale.B: Randomised same-person matched meals and sensitivity analysis; small unmasked study, allocation concealment and prospective endpoint protections not fully established.
rationale.P: Clear direction across tested contrasts; small cohort, mean/SEM and three-hour horizon limit transferable magnitude.
rationale.R: One verified exact three-condition dataset. Earlier same-team pilot is referenced but not independently appraised here; no credit inferred.

records.admissionRationale: Do not reverse the prior governed PM2 selection merely because a later discovery list contains this study. Retain the acute result as evidence and request a bounded PM2 admission decision.
records.implementationStatus: Proposed only; no canonical admission, score pin or public presentation changed

moa.description: Delayed gastric emptying and altered absorption are hypotheses; neither was measured in this experiment.
moa.evidenceQualification: Observed endpoint does not identify causal mediation; no collapsed mechanism summary proposed.

biologicalRelationship.measuredEffect: Glucose iAUC 53.4% lower versus carbohydrate first and 44.1% lower versus sandwich; incremental peak 53.8% lower versus carbohydrate first.
biologicalRelationship.pmRelevance: Acute excursion is relevant to post-meal swings, but current PM2 selects variability-specific protocols; PM1 appearance flux is also not measured.

limitations.text: 16 adults with overweight/obesity, metformin-treated T2DM; one meal composition.
Glucagon excursions did not differ; insulin and GLP-1 did not consistently differ versus sandwich.
At 180 minutes glucose was lower in carbohydrate-first; no observation beyond three hours.
Gastric emptying and nutrient appearance flux were not measured.
Acute excursion is not established day-to-day MAGE, clinical benefit or brain benefit.

records.intervention: Ten-minute walks after each main meal
records.proposition: In adults with type 2 diabetes, two weeks of advice to walk ten minutes after each meal lowered post-meal glucose iAUC versus advice to take one daily thirty-minute walk.
records.studyContext: 42 randomised, 41 completed; crossover with 30-day washout. Walk starts within five minutes of meal completion. Concealed computer allocation; unmasked intervention, blinded statistician, order-adjusted intention-to-treat models; accelerometry and seven-day CGM.

rationale.D: Exact advice-versus-advice iAUC outcome directly tested.
rationale.B: Concealed allocation, blinded analyst and order model; unmasked free-living behaviour and activity differences remain.
rationale.P: CI permits approximately 1–22% reduction, materially varying magnitude.
rationale.R: One exact advice/protocol dataset; other exercise protocols are not interchangeable replication.

records.admissionRationale: Explicit PM2 scope adjudication required. Do not relabel reduced exposure as demonstrated variability improvement.
records.implementationStatus: Proposed only; no canonical admission, score pin or public presentation changed

moa.description: Activity-related glucose utilisation is plausible, but muscle uptake and mediation were not directly quantified.
moa.evidenceQualification: Observed endpoint does not identify causal mediation; no collapsed mechanism summary proposed.

biologicalRelationship.measuredEffect: All-meal iAUC ratio 0.88 (95% CI 0.78–0.99); dinner ratio 0.78 (0.67–0.91).
biologicalRelationship.pmRelevance: Postprandial exposure supports a bounded metabolic relationship; the measured variability outcomes do not support a positive PM2 variability claim.

limitations.text: MAGE difference −0.42 mmol/L (−0.94 to 0.10), CONGA and glycaemic range were not significant; mean glucose also unchanged.
Actual activity increased despite equal prescribed minutes; timing alone was not isolated.
Interstitial glucose concentration, not appearance/disposal flux.
Short free-living T2DM trial; no cognitive outcome.

evidenceSource.studyContext: 42 randomised, 41 completed; crossover with 30-day washout. Walk starts within five minutes of meal completion. Concealed computer allocation; unmasked intervention, blinded statistician, order-adjusted intention-to-treat models; accelerometry and seven-day CGM.

records.proposition: In the fermented-food arm of the Wastyk trial, 19 of 93 measured serum inflammatory proteins decreased over the ten-week intervention; this is an exploratory within-arm observation.
records.studyContext: 18 analysed per arm, generally healthy adults; four-week ramp to about six fermented-food servings/day and six-week maintenance; high-fibre active comparator, no usual-diet control. Two fibre participants not randomised. Serial immune profiling with multiple-testing corrections.

rationale.D: Direct measurement of the explicitly observational within-arm protein proposition.
rationale.B: Repeated sampling and multiplicity control; no usual-diet control and unmasked exploratory analyses leave attribution concerns.
rationale.P: Small arm and heterogeneous exploratory markers; precise transferable effect not established.
rationale.R: One trial; multiple assays and microbiota associations are not independent replication.

records.admissionRationale: Recommend only the bounded, exploratory cytokine-marker intervention on BRS3-FM3-PM7; author review before canonical integration. No clinical efficacy claim.
records.implementationStatus: Proposed only; no canonical admission, score pin or public presentation changed

moa.description: Microbial and food-metabolite pathways remain hypotheses; the trial does not isolate a causal organism, compound or pathway.
moa.evidenceQualification: Observed endpoint does not identify causal mediation; no collapsed mechanism summary proposed.

biologicalRelationship.measuredEffect: 19/93 serum proteins decreased, including IL-6, IL-10 and IL-12b; microbiota diversity increased as a separate endpoint.
biologicalRelationship.pmRelevance: Serum immune signalling relates to cytokine network modulation. Do not automatically admit the same pattern to BRS5-FM2-PM4: diversity alone does not establish ecological selection or substrate-processing improvement.

limitations.text: Primary cytokine response score was not significant in either arm; ex vivo signalling capacity was unchanged.
No significant cognition, well-being or standard metabolic-marker changes reported.
No non-intervention control, modest sample, unmasked team and exploratory outcomes.
Diversity did not establish causal mediation of immune effects; IL-10 is not simply a harmful pro-inflammatory marker.
Mixed fermented foods; no isolated yogurt/kimchi efficacy or universal six-serving prescription.
Transient bloating during ramp-up.

evidenceSource.studyContext: 18 analysed per arm, generally healthy adults; four-week ramp to about six fermented-food servings/day and six-week maintenance; high-fibre active comparator, no usual-diet control. Two fibre participants not randomised. Serial immune profiling with multiple-testing corrections.

records.proposition: In the tested young-adult cohort, extracted potato resistant-starch supplementation was associated with higher faecal butyrate concentration during supplementation than baseline.
records.studyContext: 174 analysed across four supplements; potato n=43, ages 17–29. Random group assignment over four academic-semester studies. Three/four baseline and intervention stools; 4–7-day dose ramp then full-dose sampling. 40–48 g potato flour/day, about 70% RS2, not heated. Analysts masked; participants masked only first semester.

rationale.B: Random allocation, blinded sample analysis and repeated sampling; masking, diet and exclusions limit causal attribution.
rationale.P: Mean response established but broad dispersion and nonresponders prevent reliable individual effect size.
rationale.R: Separate academic-semester samples in one research programme provide partial confirmation; not independent-team replication.

records.admissionRationale: Recommend exact preparation-specific supplement only; do not convert existing food edges into equivalent effective-dose interventions.
records.implementationStatus: Proposed only; no canonical admission, score pin or public presentation changed

moa.description: Resistant substrate fermentation and cross-feeding are biologically supported, but species-response correlations do not isolate causal mediation of individual butyrate changes.
moa.evidenceQualification: Observed endpoint does not identify causal mediation; no collapsed mechanism summary proposed.

biologicalRelationship.measuredEffect: Potato-arm faecal butyrate increased about 29%; 63% increased and 37% were unchanged or decreased.
biologicalRelationship.pmRelevance: SCFA-related dietary substrate intervention fits PM5 with a faecal-concentration boundary, not a guaranteed barrier/brain effect.

limitations.text: Faecal concentration is not production flux, epithelial exposure or brain signalling.
Extracted unheated RS2 supplement; not cooked/cooled potato meals or a verified equivalent banana dose.
Maize resistant starch and inulin did not significantly raise butyrate; no alpha-diversity change.
Small supplement groups, incompletely masked participants, background diet uncontrolled and sample-completeness exclusions.
Individual microbiota-dependent heterogeneity; universal response is unsupported.

evidenceSource.studyContext: 174 analysed across four supplements; potato n=43, ages 17–29. Random group assignment over four academic-semester studies. Three/four baseline and intervention stools; 4–7-day dose ramp then full-dose sampling. 40–48 g potato flour/day, about 70% RS2, not heated. Analysts masked; participants masked only first semester.

records.intervention: Six-hour early eating window with weight-maintenance feeding
records.proposition: In eight men with prediabetes completing the crossover, five weeks of early six-hour feeding reduced the OGTT-derived incremental insulin/glucose AUC ratio compared with a twelve-hour eating schedule.
records.studyContext: 12 enrolled, eight completers; randomised concealed allocation, approximately seven-week washout. Matched calories/composition, supervised meals, dinner by 15:00. Completer mixed models include sequence and period; fasting duration before testing differed.

rationale.D: Direct assessment of the named OGTT-derived index, not direct disposal.
rationale.B: Concealed randomisation and matched supervised intake; completer analysis, unmasking and unequal pretest fast leave concerns.
rationale.P: Eight completers, SEM and surrogate endpoint constrain magnitude/generalisation.
rationale.R: One exact protocol trial; other fasting windows are not automatically replication.

records.admissionRationale: Recommend tightly qualified prediabetes protocol on PM3 only, retaining surrogate, fasting and population restrictions.
records.implementationStatus: Proposed only; no canonical admission, score pin or public presentation changed

moa.description: Early timing and prolonged fasting may alter metabolic handling; neither circadian mediation nor intracellular insulin signalling was isolated.
moa.evidenceQualification: Observed endpoint does not identify causal mediation; no collapsed mechanism summary proposed.

biologicalRelationship.pmRelevance: Insulin-response index is relevant to PM3, with surrogate limitations; no automatic transfer to hormonal/circadian PMs or glucose-disposal flux.

limitations.text: OGTT-derived index, not clamp disposal, tissue signalling or a directly measured circadian mechanism.
Fasting and OGTT glucose unchanged; hs-CRP, IL-6 and cortisol unchanged.
Eight male completers, unmasked supervised efficacy trial; four withdrawals.
Eating-window duration and early timing coupled; pretest fast unmatched. Sequence/period effects affected some other outcomes, not the selected index.
Fasting triglycerides and total cholesterol increased; not a uniformly beneficial metabolic profile.
Highly supervised protocol does not establish general feasibility or an unsupervised fasting prescription.

evidenceSource.studyContext: 12 enrolled, eight completers; randomised concealed allocation, approximately seven-week washout. Matched calories/composition, supervised meals, dinner by 15:00. Completer mixed models include sequence and period; fasting duration before testing differed.

records.proposition: Verified phytase dephytinisation increased iron absorption from the tested water-reconstituted cereal porridges, with material-specific exceptions.

rationale.D: The measured isotope endpoint matches the bounded absorption proposition.
rationale.B: Within-participant labelled comparisons and measured phytate; sequential meal order and unreported masking leave residual concerns.
rationale.P: Reported paired ratios support direction; small cohorts and material-dependent magnitudes prevent a precise transferable effect.
rationale.R: Separate study cohorts within the same research programme provide partial confirmation; not independent-team replication.

sources.contradictoryAssessment: No generic household soaking claim. Milk matrices and high-tannin sorghum did not consistently respond. No dopamine outcome. Separate study cohorts within the same research programme provide partial confirmation; not independent-team replication.

limitations: Milk matrices and high-tannin sorghum did not consistently respond.
records.admissionRationale: Retain existing narrowly bounded upstream iron-provision admission; no new downstream or food-generalisation claim. Shared PM4/PM5 relationships do not inherit this PM3 score.
records.implementationStatus: Already admitted and independently scored; immutable record and pin unchanged. No duplicate assessment.
